ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) of the rhombus \(ABCD\) are on the coordinate axes. If the coordinates of point \(B\) are \((-1, 0)\) and \(\angle BCD = 120^\circ\), what are the coordinates of point \(D\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that point B has the coordinates $(-1,0)$,\\
thus OB=1,\\
in diamond $ABCD$, $\angle BCD=120^\circ$, $\angle ABC+\angle BCD=180^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, $\angle BAD=120^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAC=30^\circ$, $\angle DAO=90^\circ$,\\
thus AB=2OB=2,\\
thus OA$=\sqrt{AB^{2}-OB^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}}=\sqrt{3}$,\\
since AD=AB=2,\\
thus the coordinates of point D are $\boxed{(2,\sqrt{3})}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) of the rhombus \(ABCD\) are on the coordinate axes. If the coordinates of point \(B\) are \((-1, 0)\) and \(\angle BCD = 120^\circ\), what are the coordinates of point \(D\)?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that point B has the coordinates $(-1,0)$,\\
thus OB=1,\\
in diamond $ABCD$, $\angle BCD=120^\circ$, $\angle ABC+\angle BCD=180^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, $\angle BAD=120^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAC=30^\circ$, $\angle DAO=90^\circ$,\\
thus AB=2OB=2,\\
thus OA$=\sqrt{AB^{2}-OB^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}}=\sqrt{3}$,\\
since AD=AB=2,\\
thus the coordinates of point D are $\boxed{(2,\sqrt{3})}$
